items.title: Dixie Curling Centre Turns Newcomers Into Curlers With a Five-Week Crash Course
items.summary: According to INsauga, curling is drawing growing interest across Ontario, partly thanks to its Olympic profile and rising accessibility, and Mississauga's Dixie Curling Centre at Applewood Heights Park has built its programming around welcoming people who have never tried the sport. INsauga reports the six-sheet facility runs programs 14 hours a day, seven days a week during curling season, offering everything from beginner lessons to novice, junior and advanced men's, women's and mixed leagues. The centre's adult Learn-to-Curl program is a five-week course where instructors provide all the necessary equipment, including grippers, sliders, brooms and delivery sticks, and teach delivery, sweeping, basic strategy and etiquette. INsauga notes the centre also runs a Little Rocks program for kids as young as seven, offering two hours of on-ice instruction and gameplay plus snacks, with a path toward bonspiels and competitive teams. That youth program costs under $300 for 20 weeks of two-hour weekly sessions, making it one of the more affordable ways for young Mississauga residents to try the sport.

items.title: A Logistics Fight With the City Sinks Port Credit's First-Ever Renaissance Faire Before It Opens
items.summary: According to INsauga, the Port Credit Renaissance Faire, which was set to bring medieval combat, horses, birds of prey and vendors to Port Credit Memorial Park on Aug. 29 and 30, has been cancelled before it ever took place. INsauga reports the event would have marked the first time a Renaissance faire was held in Mississauga, but the organizer said logistical issues with the City of Mississauga forced her to pull the plug. She told INsauga she called the city directly to cancel, describing a breakdown over working out the logistical and financial requirements needed to hold the event, including rules around a mobile business licence for vendors. INsauga reports the organizer said unanticipated additional costs became difficult to absorb on top of other expenses like park rental, insurance, fuel and advertising. She said she had already spent money on advertising and had lined up vendors who were interested in taking part before the cancellation.

items.title: A Mississauga 16-Year-Old's Healthcare Nonprofit Now Reaches 106 Countries
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga teenager Adil Mukhi has built a global organization called Dr. Interested that helps students explore careers in healthcare and medical research, and the group is holding a conference in Mississauga this weekend for local youth. INsauga reports the organization now reaches 106 countries and has impacted more than 160,000 people, according to Mukhi, who serves as its founder and managing director. Mukhi, now 16 and entering Grade 12 in the International Baccalaureate program at Glenforest Secondary School, started Dr. Interested when he was just 13 years old and in Grade 9. INsauga reports the idea grew out of his own experience in Grade 7 and 8, when he felt career education was limited during pandemic lockdowns and had to explore future career paths largely on his own with the help of a few mentors. One mentor helped him pursue his own interest in a healthcare career, and Mukhi said he realized many other students didn't have that kind of guidance, which is what led him to start the organization. “But I realized a lot of people didn't have this, and so that's what the organization came out of, as a way to help people learn about careers,” he said.

items.title: Rathwood's 20-Storey Rental Tower Would Gain a 144-Unit Neighbour Under New Proposal
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the City of Mississauga is reviewing an application to amend the official plan and zoning bylaw to allow a new 13-storey rental apartment building with 144 units at 1315 Bough Beeches Blvd. in the Rathwood neighbourhood, near Dixie and Rathburn roads. Mississauga.com reports the site already contains a 20-storey rental tower with 270 units, described in the applicant's planning report as a tower-in-the-park building surrounded by two surface parking lots, and that existing tower would remain in place under the proposal. The site's open space, including mature trees, a tennis court, a basketball court and a ramp to the underground parking garage, would also be preserved except for some of the surface parking. The application, prepared by WND Associates Ltd., notes the surrounding area includes one- and two-storey homes on Poltava Crescent to the north, Rathburn Road and the aging single-storey Rockwood Mall strip plaza to the south, a mid-rise apartment building and homes to the east, and a subdivision of townhouses and detached homes near Dixie Road to the west. Under the plan, the new building's residential units would occupy floors two through 13, while the ground floor would house the lobby, amenity spaces and loading and servicing areas.

items.title: Average Home in Mississauga Now Sells for Under $900,000 as Prices Keep Sliding
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, citing new data from the Toronto Regional Real Estate Board, the average home price in Mississauga fell 11.4 per cent year-over-year to $899,002 in July 2026. Mississauga.com reports the city recorded 500 home sales in July, with homes spending an average of 32 days on the market before selling, while 2,518 listings remained active by the end of the month. The board's breakdown showed 184 detached houses sold during the month, averaging 28 days on the market with 945 active listings, alongside 69 semi-detached sales averaging 26 days on the market and 204 active listings, and 23 attached house sales averaging 31 days on the market with 62 active listings. Townhouse-style condos saw their average price slide to $712,285, down roughly 2 per cent both month-over-month and year-over-year, on 95 sales that averaged 31 days on the market with 406 active listings by month's end. Mississauga.com reports the figures point to a broader cooling across most segments of the city's housing market in July.

items.title: Nick Nurse's Lawyer Says Ontario Got the Tax Ruling Wrong, and the Coach Wants His $697,500 Back
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, former Toronto Raptors head coach Nick Nurse and his wife Roberta are appealing to have $697,500 in taxes returned to them by the Ontario government, taxes they paid on their former Mississauga home under the province's Non-Resident Speculation Tax. The Star reports the couple argue they legally qualified for a rebate of the levy, which is designed to discourage foreign speculation in Ontario's housing market, but were told by the Ministry of Finance that they failed to meet residency requirements. The couple's lawyer, Mike Collinge, told the Star that Nurse and his wife are simply following the appeal process set out in the Land Transfer Tax Act to challenge a disallowance decision they believe is incorrect. The Star reports the Ministry of Finance did not respond to questions about the case. Nurse, who is from Iowa, joined the Raptors in 2013 and coached the team to its first NBA championship in 2019, before being fired in April 2023 after a season in which Toronto missed the playoffs. He was hired as head coach of the Philadelphia 76ers less than two months later.
